application.name: @gftdcojp/spirit-in-physics
application.description: Jung's Word Association Test Embedding Model for quantifying the human spirit.

processes.name: Consent & Permissions
processes.description: Handles user consent for research, audio playback, and video recording before the experiment begins.
steps: User agrees to the overall research terms.
User separately consents to audio playback and video recording permissions.

processes.name: Data Collection (2 Sessions)
processes.description: Core process where the user performs the word association test. Audio and video are recorded for later batch analysis.
steps: User clicks a button to start the session.
A stimulus word audio is played.
User has a fixed 6-second window to speak their response.
The process repeats for all words in the session.
After the first session, a break screen is shown.
The user starts the second session.
After the second session, the user is directed to the results page.

processes.name: Backend Batch Analysis
processes.description: Asynchronous process where the collected audio and video data are analyzed by Hume AI.
steps: Recorded audio/video files are uploaded to a secure storage.
A batch processing job is submitted to Hume AI.
Hume AI analyzes expression, emotion, and transcribes speech.
The results are stored in the database, linked to the user's session.

components.name: PageClient
components.description: Main client-side component orchestrating the page flow.

components.name: JungVoiceTest
components.description: Handles the entire data collection flow: consent checks, intro, two-session test loop, breaks, and recording. Manages state via `kawasakiStore`.

components.name: kawasakiStore
components.description: Zustand store for global state management. Manages the session state (e.g., current session number, word index) and stores the recorded data locally before batch processing.

steps.action: User provides all necessary consents (research, audio, video).
Audio/video recording starts. A loop begins for Session 1.
(Loop) Stimulus audio for the current word is played.
(Loop) User speaks. A 6-second timer runs. The response is recorded locally.
When Session 1 ends, a break screen is displayed. Recording is paused.
Session 2 loop starts, identical to Session 1.
When Session 2 ends, recording stops. User is shown the results page.
Recorded data is sent for asynchronous batch processing via Hume AI.

troubleshooting.issue: Real-time speech-to-text was slow and introduced latency.
troubleshooting.resolution: Changed the architecture to a data collection model. The app now records all user responses (audio/video) locally and sends them for asynchronous batch processing. This decouples the user experience from API latency.

troubleshooting.issue: Cross-browser voice recognition inconsistency and API errors.
troubleshooting.resolution: Replaced the browser's native Web Speech API with the Hume AI SDK. All API-related issues were resolved by consulting the official documentation and sample code to use the latest, correct methods for authentication and data transmission.

troubleshooting.issue: Microphone access and audio playback errors.
troubleshooting.resolution: Ensured that microphone access and audio playback are initiated by direct user actions (button clicks), complying with modern browser security policies.

troubleshooting.issue: Complex component state and React lifecycle errors.
troubleshooting.resolution: Centralized all application state into a `zustand` global store. Refactored components to be stateless where possible and use `useCallback` for functions passed into `useEffect` to prevent lifecycle issues.
